claim: The technique records the planar beating of tethered mouse sperm at high resolution.
source: We record the planar beating of tethered mouse sperm at high resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a methodological approach used in the study.

claim: Beating waveforms are reconstructed using proper orthogonal decomposition of the centerline tangent-angle profiles.
source: Beating waveforms are reconstructed using proper orthogonal decomposition of the centerline tangent-angle profiles.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a methodological approach.

claim: Energy conservation is employed to obtain the mechanical power exerted by the dynein motors from the observed kinematics.
source: Energy conservation is employed to obtain the mechanical power exerted by the dynein motors from the observed kinematics.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a methodological approach.

claim: A large proportion of the mechanical power exerted by the dynein motors is dissipated internally by the motors themselves.
source: A large proportion of the mechanical power exerted by the dynein motors is dissipated internally by the motors themselves.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract based on the analysis performed.

claim: There could be significant dissipation within the passive structures of the flagellum.
source: There could also be significant dissipation within the passive structures of the flagellum.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract with speculative language ('could').

claim: The total internal dissipation is considerably greater than the hydrodynamic dissipation in the aqueous medium outside.
source: The total internal dissipation is considerably greater than the hydrodynamic dissipation in the aqueous medium outside.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract based on the analysis performed.

claim: The net power input from the dynein motors in sperm from Crisp2-knockout mice is significantly smaller than in wildtype samples.
source: The net power input from the dynein motors in sperm from Crisp2-knockout mice is significantly smaller than in wildtype samples, indicating that ion-channel regulation by cysteine-rich secretory proteins controls energy flows powering the axoneme.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract based on comparative analysis of WT and KO samples.

claim: Ion-channel regulation by cysteine-rich secretory proteins controls energy flows powering the axoneme.
source: The net power input from the dynein motors in sperm from Crisp2-knockout mice is significantly smaller than in wildtype samples, indicating that ion-channel regulation by cysteine-rich secretory proteins controls energy flows powering the axoneme.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings in the abstract.

claim: Sperm propel themselves by beating a whip-like flagellum in their journey towards the oocyte.
source: In their journey towards the oocyte, sperm propel themselves by beating a whip-like flagellum.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Sperm motility is essential for successful fertilization and is fundamental to reproduction.
source: This motility is essential for successful fertilization and is fundamental to reproduction.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Understanding sperm motility is essential for improving male infertility treatments, animal breeding, and wildlife conservation.
source: Understanding sperm motility is essential for improving male infertility treatments, animal breeding, and wildlife conservation (Gaffney et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: The mechanisms that control the complex beating patterns observed in flagella remain poorly understood.
source: the mechanisms that control the complex beating patterns observed in flagella remain poorly understood (Brokaw, 2009; Lehti and Sironen, 2017; Lindemann and Lesich, 2016; Lin and Nicastro, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations supporting the claim.

claim: Mechanical properties of the flagellum and its surroundings play a crucial role in determining sperm motility.
source: It is, however, recognized that mechanical properties of the flagellum and its surroundings play a crucial role in determining sperm motility (Gaffney et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Measurements of the mechanical behavior of single flagella in living sperm have remained a critical bottleneck.
source: Measurements of the mechanical behavior of single flagella in living sperm have however remained a critical bottleneck.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a motivation for the study.

claim: Automated image-analysis tools have long been used to study sperm movement.
source: Automated image-analysis tools have long been used to study sperm movement (Katz et al., 1975; Katz and Overstreet, 1981; Overstreet et al., 1979).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Computer-aided sperm analysis systems are used extensively in clinical settings to rapidly assess the viability of samples containing hundreds of cells in a single field of view.
source: Computer-aided sperm analysis systems are today used extensively in clinical settings to rapidly assess the viability of samples containing hundreds of cells in a single field of view (FOV) (Amann and Waberski, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: High-throughput computer-aided sperm analysis techniques do not resolve flagellar motion.
source: These high-throughput techniques, however, do not resolve flagellar motion.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of existing techniques.

claim: Improvements in digital imaging and storage have placed within reach the high-speed, high-resolution, and long-exposure imaging that researchers of flagellar propulsion have long sought.
source: Improvements in digital imaging and storage have now placed within reach the high-speed, high-resolution, and long-exposure imaging that researchers of flagellar propulsion have long sought (Gray, 1955; Gray, 1958; Brokaw, 1966; Rikmenspoel et al., 1960).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The study implemented image-analysis techniques to automatically extract centerlines of sperm flagella in every video frame.
source: We have implemented these image-analysis techniques to automatically extract centerlines of sperm flagella in every video frame.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a methodological contribution.

claim: The study images swimming sperm over several beat cycles to quantitatively analyze beat patterns in a statistically meaningful way.
source: To quantitatively analyze beat patterns in a statistically meaningful way, we need to image swimming sperm over several beat cycles.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a methodological requirement.

claim: It is unlikely that sufficient beat cycles can be reliably recorded with freely swimming sperm that can quickly move out of focal plane or the field of view.
source: While rapid progress is being made on full three-dimensional tracking (Muschol et al., 2018; Dardikman-Yoffe et al., 2020; Gadêlha et al., 2019), it is unlikely that sufficient beat cycles can be reliably recorded with freely swimming sperm that can quickly move out of focal plane or the FOV (Mondal et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations, explaining the rationale for using tethered cells.

claim: The study images flagella beating freely in the focal plane in cells tethered chemically at their heads to a glass slide.
source: Instead, we image flagella beating freely in the focal plane in cells tethered chemically at their heads to a glass slide.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as the experimental approach.

claim: The tethered-cell assay permits imaging single cells until they stop beating.
source: Our tethered-cell assay, in principle, permits imaging single cells until they stop beating.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an advantage of the method.

claim: The study reports results obtained by analyzing large numbers of (~50) beat cycles in single tethered sperm in freshly prepared samples when they are most vigorous.
source: We report here results obtained by analyzing large numbers of (∼50) beat cycles in single tethered sperm in freshly prepared samples when they are most vigorous (Gaikwad et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the data analyzed.

claim: Beating patterns in sperm flagella have been studied previously to investigate changes induced by environmental factors.
source: Beating patterns in sperm flagella have been studied previously to investigate changes induced by environmental factors (Bukatin et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2009; Saggiorato et al., 2017) or by gene mutations (Krähling et al., 2013; Lim et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Beating patterns in sperm flagella have been studied previously to investigate changes induced by gene mutations.
source: Beating patterns in sperm flagella have been studied previously to investigate changes induced by environmental factors (Bukatin et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2009; Saggiorato et al., 2017) or by gene mutations (Krähling et al., 2013; Lim et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The technique of proper orthogonal decomposition can be applied on the time-resolved tangent-angle profiles of flagellar centerlines to analyze their kinematics.
source: We build here on the suggestion that the technique of proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) can be applied on the time-resolved tangent-angle profiles of flagellar centerlines to analyze their kinematics (Ma et al., 2014; Werner et al., 2014; Saggiorato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: POD is widely applied in the analysis of turbulent flows and other fields to reduce complexity of spatiotemporal patterns.
source: POD is widely applied in the analysis of turbulent flows (Lumley, 1967; Holmes et al., 2012) and other fields (Baumberg and Hogg, 1994; Jolliffe, 2002) to reduce complexity of spatiotemporal patterns and represent them with a much smaller set of numbers, while still retaining accuracy.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The study applies POD to unambiguously identify the mean beat cycle of each sperm from the time series of the tangent-angle profiles of its flagellar centerline.
source: To objectively compare flagellar beating patterns, we apply POD to unambiguously identify the mean beat cycle of each sperm from the time series of the tangent-angle profiles of its flagellar centerline.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a methodological contribution.

claim: The study introduces a technique to consistently represent the POD shape modes with smooth Chebyshev polynomials.
source: We further introduce a technique to consistently represent the POD shape modes with smooth Chebyshev polynomials to ensure that the tangent-angle profile is sufficiently smooth and its spatial derivatives can be computed without spurious artifacts.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a methodological contribution.

claim: The tangent-angle profile obtained with the Chebyshev-POD technique is consistent with the rigid-body kinematics of the stiff head region.
source: The tangent-angle profile obtained thus is consistent with the rigid-body kinematics of the stiff head region.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a feature of the method.

claim: The Chebyshev-POD technique allows for efficient calculation of geometric quantities such as the local curvature and kinematic quantities such as the velocity components at any material point on the centerline.
source: This Chebyshev-POD (C-POD) technique allows for efficient calculation of geometric quantities such as the local curvature and kinematic quantities such as the velocity components, at any material point on the centerline.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an advantage of the method.

claim: The approach for calculating forces and energetics from the measured beating patterns stems from ideas discussed originally by Machin, 1963.
source: Our approach for calculating forces and energetics from the measured beating patterns stems from ideas discussed originally by Machin, 1963.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: The study uses geometric and kinematic data to determine the hydrodynamic resistance offered by the external fluid medium using resistive force theory.
source: We use the geometric and kinematic data to determine the hydrodynamic resistance offered by the external fluid medium using resistive force theory (RFT) (Gray and Hancock, 1955; Lighthill, 1976) and further calculate internal forces by applying conservation principles.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The study proposes a Soft-Internally-Driven-Kirchhoff-Rod (SIDKR) model that is agnostic to the nature of motor activity and avoids invoking the assumption that the flagellar material is active.
source: We propose instead a different approach that is agnostic to the nature of motor activity and avoids invoking the assumption that the flagellar material is active.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a novel modeling approach.

claim: The SIDKR model leads to an energy balance across the flagellum, which is used to determine the spatiotemporal distribution of motor power across the flagellum over its mean cycle.
source: The resulting Soft-Internally -Driven-Kirchhoff-Rod (SIDKR) model leads to an energy balance across the flagellum, which we then use to determine the spatiotemporal distribution of motor power across the flagellum over its mean cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a methodological contribution.

claim: The study analyzed flagellar beating patterns of sperm from wildtype and Crisp2 knockout mice.
source: We have used this approach to analyze flagellar beating patterns of sperm from wildtype (WT) and Crisp2 knockout (KO) mice.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the experimental samples.

claim: The cysteine-rich secretory proteins (CRISPs) are a group of proteins that are predominantly expressed in the male reproductive tract.
source: The cysteine-rich secretory proteins (CRISPs) are a group of proteins that are predominantly expressed in the male reproductive tract (Gaikwad et al., in preparation).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: Crisp2 is incorporated into the sperm acrosome, connecting piece and the outer dense fibers of the sperm tail.
source: Crisp2 is incorporated into the sperm acrosome, connecting piece and the outer dense fibers of the sperm tail.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: The deletion of Crisp2 in mice leads to compromised sperm function, including altered sperm motility.
source: It is known that the deletion of Crisp2 in mice leads to compromised sperm function, including altered sperm motility (Hu et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The precise effect of Crisp2 deletion on flagellar function is unknown.
source: The precise effect on flagellar function, however, is unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a knowledge gap.

claim: There is considerable intracellular friction within the flagellum.
source: Our observations with these sperm reveal intriguing new information: there is considerable intracellular friction within the flagellum.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a key finding.

claim: The hydrodynamic resistance offered by the viscous fluid medium outside is widely held to be the sole dissipative sink that must be overcome by the continual driving provided by the dynein motors.
source: This challenges the widely held view that the hydrodynamic resistance offered by the viscous fluid medium outside is the sole dissipative sink that must be overcome by the continual driving provided by the dynein motors.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a prevailing view being challenged.

claim: The flagellar filament is conventionally regarded as an elastic body that perfectly stores energy temporarily by bending.
source: Further, the flagellar filament is also conventionally regarded as an elastic body that perfectly stores energy temporarily by bending.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conventional view.

claim: Internal friction within the passive structures of the flagellum, and within the motors themselves, may be as large as the external hydrodynamic friction.
source: Our findings suggest instead that internal friction within the passive structures of the flagellum, and within the motors themselves, may be as large as the external hydrodynamic friction.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a key finding.

claim: The findings are in line with recent observations made in algal cilia.
source: These are in line with recent observations also made in algal cilia (Mondal et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: Internal sources of dissipation could play a significant role in determining beating patterns in sperm.
source: These sources of internal dissipation could therefore play a significant role in determining beating patterns in sperm (Camalet and Jülicher, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: This insight could be vital for understanding dramatic changes in flagellar beating patterns induced by changes in the medium or the proximity of surfaces.
source: This insight could be vital for understanding dramatic changes in flagellar beating patterns induced by changes in the medium (Smith et al., 2009) or the proximity of surfaces (Nosrati et al., 2015; Denissenko et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The sperm body is treated as a slender, flexible filament immersed in a viscous fluid.
source: The sperm body is treated as a slender, flexible filament immersed in a viscous fluid (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the theoretical model section and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The passive material of the sperm body is assumed to be a Kirchhoff rod.
source: It is assumed that the passive material of the sperm body is a Kirchhoff rod (Audoly and Pomeau, 2010; Malvern, 1969; O'Reilly, 2017), that is, it is inextensible and each of its material cross-sections remains rigid and planar, while rotating with respect to each other about the rod axis as it bends and twists.
evidence: This is stated in the theoretical model section with citations.

claim: The passive Kirchhoff rod is driven by axonemal motors acting on its internal surfaces.
source: It is driven by axonemal motors acting on its internal surfaces and the resulting motion is resisted by the hydrodynamic forces that act on its external surface (Figure 1) as well as the stresses that arise to resist material deformation as the rod bends.
evidence: This is stated in the theoretical model section and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The head is assumed to be a rigid body.
source: We assume that the head is a rigid body.
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section.

claim: Cells are tethered at a point in the head region, and the head can rotate rigidly about this tether point.
source: In our experiments, cells are further tethered at a point in the head region, and the head can rotate rigidly about this tether point.
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section.

claim: The head does not contain internal motors, which are all distributed only along the tail region.
source: The head does not contain internal motors, which are all distributed only along the tail region.
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section.

claim: Each dynein motor is assumed to act on the internal surfaces of a cross-section such that the forces exerted at its two ends are of equal magnitude but in opposite directions.
source: In the flagellar tail, each dynein motor is assumed to act on the internal surfaces of a cross-section such that the forces exerted at its two ends are of equal magnitude but in opposite directions.
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section.

claim: The external hydrodynamic force distribution is given by resistive force theory.
source: The external hydrodynamic force distribution is given by RFT (Gray and Hancock, 1955; Lighthill, 1976):
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section with citations.

claim: For sperm tethered to a glass slide, the no-slip condition at the slide surface creates an additional resistance to fluid flow.
source: For sperm tethered to a glass slide, the no-slip condition at the slide surface creates an additional resistance to fluid flow.
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section.

claim: The friction coefficients from Katz et al. have been used in a number of previous studies.
source: These coefficients have previously been used in a number of studies, notably by Jülicher and co-workers (Riedel-Kruse et al., 2007) for analyzing experimental data on wall-tethered sperm and, more recently, by Mondal et al., 2020, for tethered axonemes isolated from cilia.
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section with citations.

claim: The simplest constitutive model for the elastic stress in a passive material is the Hookean model, which leads to a linear relation between the elastic material torque and the local curvature.
source: The simplest constitutive model for the elastic stress in a passive material is the Hookean model, which leads to a linear relation between the elastic material torque and the local curvature.
evidence: This is stated in the constitutive relations section.

claim: The image-analysis algorithm processes videos of single sperm cells tethered to a glass surface and beating in the focal plane of the microscope.
source: Briefly, the image-analysis algorithm is used to process videos of single sperm cells tethered to a glass surface and beating in the focal plane of the microscope and extract centerlines of sperm bodies in every video frame.
evidence: This is stated in the kinematics section.

claim: Twentieth-order Chebyshev polynomials are fitted through centerlines to construct smooth tangent-angle profiles of the flagellar tail region.
source: Twentieth-order Chebyshev polynomials are fitted through these centerlines to construct smooth tangent-angle profiles (see Figure 1A) of the flagellar tail region.
evidence: This is stated in the kinematics section and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: These Chebyshev polynomials are designed to be consistent with the rigid-body kinematics of the head region.
source: These Chebyshev polynomials are designed to be consistent with the rigid-body kinematics of the head region.
evidence: This is stated in the kinematics section.

claim: POD is an order-reduction technique that optimally approximates spatiotemporally varying data.
source: In general, the POD is an order-reduction technique that optimally approximates spatiotemporally varying data.
evidence: This is stated in the kinematics section.

claim: There are few measurements of the bending stiffness for sperm flagella in the literature.
source: There are few measurements of the bending stiffness for sperm flagella in the literature.
evidence: This is stated in the dynamics and energetics section.

claim: Mouse sperm heads have distinctive falciform (hook) shapes.
source: Mouse sperm heads have distinctive falciform (hook) shapes (Woolley, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation.

claim: All video frames are initially digitally rotated or reflected such that the head is on the left end of the body with the hook facing concave downward.
source: In the image-processing protocol we have followed, all video frames are initially digitally rotated or reflected such that the head is on the left end of the body with the hook facing concave downward.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: In one outlier KO sample (KO-5), the mean shape is anti-hook concave throughout.
source: In the one outlier KO sample (KO-5) in Figure 2A, however, the mean shape is anti-hook concave throughout.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Intrinsic net asymmetry in flagellar beating is well known in sperm in many mammalian species, even when uncapacitated.
source: Intrinsic net asymmetry in flagellar beating is well known in sperm in many mammalian species, even when uncapacitated.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The observation that the mean shape is curved with an anti-hook (ventral) concave shape is consistent with the observations of Woolley, 2003 that, in mouse sperm, the flagellum bends at the neck more on the ventral side than on the other.
source: Our observation that the mean shape is curved with an anti-hook (ventral) concave shape is consistent with the observations of Woolley, 2003 that, in mouse sperm, the flagellum bends at the neck more on the ventral side than on the other.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation.

claim: Just the first two modes achieve a capture efficiency greater than 92% for all the WT samples, and for three out of the five KO samples.
source: Just the first two modes achieve a capture efficiency greater than 92% for all the WT samples, and for three out of the five KO samples.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: For the other two KO samples, the first two dominant shape modes account for more than 85% of the observed beating patterns.
source: Even for the other two KO samples these dominant shape modes account for more than 85% of the observed beating patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Across all samples, the first four modes describe at least 95% of the beating patterns.
source: Across all samples, the first four modes describe at least 95% of the beating patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: All kinematic, dynamic, and energetic quantities are calculated using the first four shape modes and their time-dependent coefficients.
source: We therefore calculate all kinematic, dynamic, and energetic quantities using the first four shape modes and their time-dependent coefficients.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: For any sperm sample, the trajectory traced out in B1-B2 phase space consists of loops, one for each beat cycle.
source: For any sperm sample, the trajectory traced out in B1-B2 phase space consists of loops, one for each beat cycle (e.g., Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In each sperm sample, the shape at the start of a beat cycle always corresponds mostly to the shape of the first dominant mode.
source: This choice means that, in each sperm sample, the shape at the start of a beat cycle always corresponds mostly to the shape of the first dominant mode (with minor contributions from modes higher than the second; Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The C-POD technique applied to tethered sperm makes it possible to systematically accumulate data for large numbers of beat cycles.
source: Although Figure 2D, E shows only a few cycles for clarity, the C-POD technique applied to tethered sperm makes it possible to systematically accumulate data for large numbers of beat cycles and quantitatively compare, in a statistically meaningful sense, individual sperm samples within a genotypical population and also compare one genotypical population with another.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Every single planar wave that propagates down the filament is associated with a pair of hydrodynamic dissipation peaks.
source: Comparing the bands in Figure 3B with those in Figure 3A, it is clear that every single planar wave that propagates down the filament is associated with a pair of hydrodynamic dissipation peaks: the contribution of any single location to the hydrodynamic dissipation peaks as the filament moves quickly while bending and relaxing back on one side, and then again, on the other side.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: This behavior of negative active power is observed consistently in all beat cycles and for all WT and KO samples.
source: We observe this behavior consistently in all beat cycles and for all WT and KO samples.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The energy transferred back as mechanical work on the motors must be quickly dissipated locally within the axoneme itself.
source: The energy transferred back as mechanical work on the motors can neither be stored either within the dyneins nor converted back to chemical free energy (i.e., ATP): it must be therefore quickly dissipated locally within the axoneme itself.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The qualitative features of the distributions of the key energetic variables are common to both WT and KO samples.
source: The qualitative features of the distributions of the key energetic variables discussed above are common to both WT and KO samples.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The difference between the mean beat patterns of the WT and Crisp2 KO samples is striking, with KO samples exhibiting a smaller amplitude across the entire flagellar tail.
source: The difference between the mean beat patterns of the WT and Crisp2 KO samples is striking. The KO samples exhibit a smaller amplitude across the entire flagellar tail.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: No distinctive common patterns are immediately apparent across the WT or KO samples in the mean cycles of energy flows.
source: No distinctive common patterns are immediately apparent across the WT or KO samples in Figure 4B.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In two of the KO samples (KO-1 and KO-5), the net motor power remains nearly constant over the entire cycle.
source: In two of the KO samples (KO-1 and KO-5), however, the net motor power remains nearly constant over the entire cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The mean cycles of the energy flows vary considerably from sample to sample.
source: It is visually apparent from Figure 4B that the mean cycles of the energy flows vary considerably from sample to sample.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: For values of η_n much smaller than 10^3 Pa s μm^4, the overall motion of the flagellum during a phase of the cycle is powered mostly by the release of the potential energy stored elastically in the body of the flagellum, which appears to be physically unrealistic.
source: The overall motion of the flagellum during that phase of the cycle is powered mostly by the release of the potential energy stored elastically in the body of the flagellum. This appears to be physically unrealistic.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Average hydrodynamic dissipation can be used as an indicator of the average motor input.
source: This suggests that average hydrodynamic dissipation, which only needs the application of RFT, can be used as an indicator of the average motor input, which requires a more involved calculation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The dissipation at the head against hydrodynamic and tethering forces is just a small fraction of the hydrodynamic dissipation across the tail region.
source: We find that the dissipation at the head against hydrodynamic and tethering forces is just a small fraction of the hydrodynamic dissipation across the tail region (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The excess of the time-averaged motor power input above the hydrodynamic dissipation is required to primarily overcome the different sources of internal dissipation in the tail.
source: Therefore, the excess of the time-averaged motor power input above the hydrodynamic dissipation is required to primarily overcome the different sources of internal dissipation in the tail.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Motor dissipation is substantial when compared with the hydrodynamic dissipation.
source: We observe in Figure 5C that motor dissipation is substantial when compared with the hydrodynamic dissipation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the KO samples, the motor dissipation (48.7 fW) is smaller than the hydrodynamic dissipation (66.3 fW), but of comparable magnitude.
source: In the KO samples, the motor dissipation (48.7 fW) is smaller than the hydrodynamic dissipation (66.3 fW), but of comparable magnitude.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In wall-tethered WT as well as Crisp2 KO mice sperm beating in an aqueous medium, the total internal dissipation due to motor and internal friction is considerably larger than the external hydrodynamic dissipation.
source: The data in Figure 5C thus leads us to conclude that, in wall-tethered WT as well as Crisp2 KO mice sperm beating in an aqueous medium, the total internal dissipation due to motor and internal friction is considerably larger than the external hydrodynamic dissipation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The net input from the dynein motors in sperm from Crisp2 KO mice is significantly smaller than the power input in the corresponding WTs.
source: We find that the net input from the dynein motors in sperm from Crisp2 KO mice is significantly smaller than the power input in the corresponding WTs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Each kind of dissipation – hydrodynamic, motor, or internal friction – is smaller in sperm from Crisp2 KO mice.
source: We further find that each kind of dissipation – hydrodynamic, motor, or internal friction – is smaller in sperm from Crisp2 KO mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The observations that each kind of dissipation is smaller in Crisp2 KO samples are consistent with the observation that the Crisp2 KO samples have smaller beating amplitudes over the entire flagellum.
source: These observations in Figure 5D are consistent with those in Figure 4A that the Crisp2 KO samples have smaller beating amplitudes over the entire flagellum.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 4A and 5D.

claim: In both genotypes, the hydrodynamic dissipation occurs primarily due to the motion of the principal piece.
source: In both genotypes, the hydrodynamic dissipation occurs primarily due to the motion of the principal piece as expected.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Most of the motor dissipation appears to occur in the mid-piece region in the WT population (average of 110 fW compared to 25.1 fW in the principal piece).
source: In contrast, most of the motor dissipation appears to occur in the mid-piece region in the WT population (average of 110 fW compared to 25.1 fW in the principal piece).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In the KO samples, motor dissipation in both mid-piece and principal piece is similar (averages of 29.1 and 19.5 fW, respectively).
source: In the KO samples, on the other hand, motor dissipation in both mid-piece and principal piece is similar (averages of 29.1 and 19.5 fW, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In the KO population, the internal dissipation in the mid-piece (32.4 fW) is much lower than in the principal piece (168 fW).
source: However, in the KO population, the internal dissipation in the mid-piece (32.4 fW) is much lower than in the principal piece (168 fW) .
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The internal dissipation in the principal piece of KO samples is higher than average internal dissipation in the KO samples, despite their more vigorous motion.
source: This latter value is also higher than average internal dissipation in the KO samples, despite their more vigorous motion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The physical significance of the spatial distribution of the motor dissipations or the variations between the WT and KO species are not clear at this stage and require further detailed investigation.
